mainTopic: How often a husband owes his wife עונה and how long he may be away learning Torah, with side discussions on sighing and on the strength of the men of ארץ ישראל.
overview: The גמרא asks how long a man may fairly be away from home learning Torah. רב says one month away and one month home, learning from דוד המלך's army rotations. רבי יוחנן says one month away and two months home, learning from the workers in the לבנון who prepared materials for the בית המקדש. Each explains why he did not use the other's פסוק. The same two אמוראים also argue whether a sigh breaks half the body or the whole body, and a story about a Jew and a gentile shows that an old, familiar sorrow does not crush like a new one. The גמרא then returns to the משנה's schedule of עונה and defines the טיילין as comfortable, worry-free men, with stories about the great strength of the men of ארץ ישראל. It explains that פועלים owe twice a week when they work in their own city and once a week when they work elsewhere. Finally, רבה בר רב חנן asks whether the one-week vow rule matters only for a טייל and a פועל, and אביי's answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: How long is the normal time away?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how long the normal, accepted amount of time away from home for Torah study is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the normal way of doing this, and how long?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question to set up the next move. It wants to know the normal, fair length of time a man may be away learning Torah before coming home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The topic is a man who goes away to learn. The גמרא is not asking about the outer legal limit. It is asking what is fair and normal, and the next two steps give two answers.

keyTerms.meaning: The normal, proper way of doing the matter

phrases.english: The normal way of the matter, how much?
phrases.notes: He means: what is a fair amount of time for the husband to be away learning Torah?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the discussion in this section.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The proper length of time a man may be away for Torah study compared with time at home.

steps.title: רב: one month away, one month home
steps.stepSummary: רב says one month in the study hall and one month at home, based on דוד המלך's army divisions.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: a month here and a month at home, as it says: 'In every matter of the divisions, which came and went month by month for all the months of the year.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives his answer: equal time, one month away and one month home. He brings a פסוק about דוד המלך's army groups that served in rotation, one month at a time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each army division served one month and then went home while another division took over. רב applies this even split to a man learning Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: A month here, meaning in the study hall
The divisions, the groups that rotated service

phrases.english: Rav said:
A month here, and a month at home.
As it is said: "In every matter of the divisions
that came in and went out month by month
for all the months of the year."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: חֹדֶשׁ כָּאן, וְחֹדֶשׁ בַּבַּיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Equal time: one month away learning, one month at home.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: one month away, two months home
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says one month away and two months at home, based on the workers who cut wood in the לבנון for the בית המקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: a month here and two at his home, as it says: 'A month they would be in the לבנון, two months at his home.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן disagrees with רב and says the man should be home twice as long as he is away. His proof is the פסוק about שלמה's workers for the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Those workers spent one month in the לבנון and two months home. רבי יוחנן uses that ratio, which gives the wife more of her husband's time than רב's view does.

keyTerms.meaning: The לבנון, where wood for the בית המקדש was cut

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
A month here and two in his home,
As it is said: "A month they would be in the Levanon,
two months at his home."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: חֹדֶשׁ כָּאן וּשְׁנַיִם בְּבֵיתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב's answer in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One month away learning, two months at home.

steps.title: Why didn't רב learn from the Temple workers?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב did not learn from רבי יוחנן's פסוק about the בית המקדש workers.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב too, what is the reason he did not say it from that one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב: there is a clear פסוק giving two months home, so why didn't he follow it? The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides used a פסוק about work done in rotation. The question is why רב picked the army model and not the בית המקדש model.

phrases.english: And Rav too, what is the reason
he did not say it from that one?
phrases.notes: "That one" is רבי יוחנן's פסוק about the workers in the Levanon.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב נָמֵי, מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר מֵהַהִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions רב's choice of source in light of step 3.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק giving two months at home exists, so רב should have followed it.

steps.title: Building the Temple could be done by others
steps.stepSummary: The בית המקדש workers could get more time off because many other people could do the job, which is not true of Torah learning.
steps.simpleTranslation: The building of the בית המקדש is different, since it is possible through others.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רב. The בית המקדש workers could rest longer because there were plenty of other workers to take over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No one can learn Torah in place of someone else, so a learner needs more time in the study hall than a builder who can be replaced. That is why רב uses the army model with an even split.

keyTerms.meaning: The building of the בית המקדש

phrases.english: The building of the Temple is different,
since it is possible through others.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The בית המקדש workers' schedule should apply to Torah learners too.
steps.terutzMaskana: Building work can be shared with others, but Torah learning cannot, so a learner gets more time away.

steps.title: Why didn't רבי יוחנן learn from the army?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן did not learn from רב's פסוק about דוד המלך's army divisions.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן, what is the reason he did not say it from that one?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא asks the same question the other way: why didn't רבי יוחנן follow the army's one-month rotation? The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This mirrors step 4. Each side has to explain why the other's פסוק does not fit a man learning Torah.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan, what is the reason
he did not say it from that one?
phrases.notes: Here "that one" is רב's פסוק about דוד's army divisions.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר מֵהַהִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel question, now directed at רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק with an even one-month rotation exists, so why not follow it?

steps.title: The soldiers earned money
steps.stepSummary: The army case is different because the soldiers made money from serving, so a wife would accept more time away.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, since he has profit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי יוחנן. The soldiers earned a living from serving the king, which is why they could be away as long as they were home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the husband brings in money, his wife is more willing to let him be away. Torah learning brings in no money, so she would want him home longer, which leads to two months at home.
steps.whatToRemember: רב says one month away and one month home, because Torah learning cannot be passed on to others. רבי יוחנן says one month away and two months home, because Torah learning earns no money, so the wife would want her husband home longer.

phrases.english: It is different there, since he has profit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The army rotation should apply to Torah learners.
steps.terutzMaskana: The soldiers earned money, so their wives would agree to more time apart. That reason does not apply to Torah learning.

steps.title: רב: a sigh breaks half the body
steps.stepSummary: רב says a sigh breaks half of a person's body, from the פסוק 'groan with the breaking of loins.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: A sigh breaks half of a person's body, as it says: 'And you, son of man, sigh with the breaking of loins, and with bitterness sigh.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new, separate מחלוקת between רב and רבי יוחנן. רב says a sigh breaks half the body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links sighing with "breaking of the loins," and the loins are the middle of the body. So רב reads it as breaking half of the body.

phrases.english: Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: אֲנָחָה שׁוֹבֶרֶת חֲצִי גּוּפוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם,
phrases.english: A sigh breaks half of a person's body,
As it is said: "And you, son of man, sigh
with the breaking of loins, and with bitterness sigh."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: אֲנָחָה שׁוֹבֶרֶת חֲצִי גּוּפוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic, brought because it is another מחלוקת between the same two אמוראים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sigh breaks half the body.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: a sigh breaks the whole body
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says a sigh breaks the entire body, from the next פסוק, which lists heart, hands, spirit and knees.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Even all of a person's body, as it says: 'And when they say to you, Why are you sighing? You shall say, Because of the news that is coming, and every heart will melt, all hands will go weak, every spirit will grow faint, and all knees will run with water.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן disagrees and says a sigh breaks the whole body. His proof is the next פסוק, which describes every part of the body falling apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The heart, hands, spirit and knees together cover the whole person, from top to bottom. So the damage is not limited to half the body.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
Even all of a person's body,
As it is said: "And it shall be, when they say to you,
Why are you sighing?
You shall say: Because of the news that is coming,

phrases.aramaic: וְנָמֵס כׇּל לֵב וְרָפוּ כׇל יָדַיִם
phrases.english: and every heart will melt, and all hands will go weak,
and every spirit will grow faint,
and all knees will run with water."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אַף כׇּל גּוּפוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sigh breaks the whole body.

steps.title: But the פסוק says 'breaking of loins'!
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן: the פסוק mentions only the loins, which suggests just half the body.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן too, isn't it written 'with the breaking of loins'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יוחנן's view using רב's פסוק. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק says the loins break, that sounds like the breaking stops halfway. That seems to contradict רבי יוחנן's claim that the whole body breaks.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan too,
isn't it written "with the breaking of loins"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן in step 9 using רב's פסוק from step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's view that the whole body breaks
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק names only the loins, which implies half the body.

steps.title: The breaking starts at the loins
steps.stepSummary: The loins are where the breaking begins, not where it ends.
steps.simpleTranslation: That one means that when it begins, it begins from the loins.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי יוחנן. The פסוק tells us where the breaking starts, not how far it goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read this way, "breaking of loins" is the starting point. The breaking can still spread to the whole body, so both פסוקים fit רבי יוחנן's view.

phrases.english: That one is that when it begins —
it begins from the loins.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The breaking reaches only the loins.
steps.terutzMaskana: The loins are only where the breaking starts. It then spreads through the whole body.

steps.title: But the next פסוק describes the whole body!
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב: the next פסוק describes heart, hands and spirit all failing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב too, isn't it written: 'and every heart will melt, all hands will go weak, every spirit will grow faint'!
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא attacks רב using רבי יוחנן's פסוק. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק clearly describes the whole body breaking down. That seems to disprove רב's limit of half the body.

phrases.english: And Rav too, isn't it written:
"And every heart will melt, and all hands will go weak,
and every spirit will grow faint"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel challenge, now against רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's view that only half the body breaks
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק describes the whole body failing.

steps.title: News of the Temple's destruction is exceptional
steps.stepSummary: The news of the בית המקדש's destruction is especially crushing, so it breaks the whole body. A normal sigh breaks only half.
steps.simpleTranslation: The news about the בית המקדש is different, since it is very crushing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רב. That פסוק is about the terrible news of the בית המקדש's destruction, which is far worse than an ordinary cause for sighing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a sigh breaks half the body. This extreme news is an exception that breaks the whole body, so the פסוק does not set the general rule.
steps.whatToRemember: רב says a normal sigh breaks half the body, and only the news of the בית המקדש's destruction breaks all of it. רבי יוחנן says a sigh breaks the whole body, starting from the loins.

phrases.english: The news of the Temple is different,
since it is very crushing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every sigh breaks the whole body.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the extreme news of the בית המקדש's destruction breaks the whole body. A normal sigh breaks half.

steps.title: A Jew and a gentile walking together
steps.stepSummary: A gentile cannot keep up with a Jew. He reminds him of the חורבן, and the Jew sighs, but the Jew still walks faster.
steps.simpleTranslation: A Jew and a gentile were walking together. The gentile could not keep up, so he reminded the Jew of the destruction of the בית המקדש. The Jew groaned and sighed, but the gentile still could not keep up with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that tests the rule from the steps before, that a sigh breaks a person's body. This story sets up the gentile's question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 said that news of the חורבן breaks the whole body. Here the Jew hears about the חורבן and sighs, yet he loses no speed. That seems to clash with what was just taught.

keyTerms.meaning: to walk along, to keep pace

phrases.english: A certain Jew and a gentile
were walking along the road together.

phrases.aramaic: לָא אִימְּצִי גּוֹי לְסַגּוֹיֵי בַּהֲדֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל.
phrases.english: The gentile could not keep pace with the Jew.
He reminded him of the destruction of the בית המקדש,
phrases.notes: The gentile is the one doing the reminding.

phrases.english: he groaned and sighed,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲפִילּוּ הָכִי לָא אִימְּצִי גּוֹי לְסַגּוֹיֵי בַּהֲדֵיהּ.
phrases.english: and even so the gentile could not keep pace with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא יִשְׂרָאֵל וְגוֹי דַּהֲווֹ קָאָזְלִי בְּאוֹרְחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the rule from step 13 with a real-life case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hearing about the חורבן did not weaken this Jew.

steps.title: The gentile asks why the sigh did not weaken him
steps.stepSummary: The gentile asks: don't you Jews say that a sigh breaks half a person's body?
steps.simpleTranslation: The gentile said to him: Don't you say that a sigh breaks half of a person's body?
steps.whatsHappening: The gentile challenges the Jew using the Jews' own teaching about sighing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a sigh breaks half the body, the Jew should have slowed down after sighing. He did not, so the teaching seems wrong.

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: לָאו אָמְרִיתוּ ״אֲנָחָה שׁוֹבֶרֶת חֲצִי גּוּפוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם״?
phrases.english: Don't you say, "A sigh breaks half of a person's body"?
phrases.notes: This is רב's view from the earlier steps, that a normal sigh breaks half the body.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises the problem created by the story in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The teaching that a sigh breaks half the body
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Jew sighed and still walked fast, so the sigh did not weaken him.

steps.title: A familiar sorrow does not crush like a new one
steps.stepSummary: The Jew answers that the rule applies only to new bad news. A sorrow people are used to does not break them, and he backs this up with a common saying.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: That applies only to a new sorrow. But this one, which we have been through again and again, does not affect us that way. As people say: a woman used to losing her children does not panic.
steps.whatsHappening: The Jew answers the gentile. A sigh breaks the body only when the sorrow is new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is not wrong, but it has a limit. The חורבן is an old pain the Jews have lived with for a long time, so remembering it does not shock the body. The saying about a mother used to loss shows that people get used to repeated pain.

keyTerms.meaning: that we have repeated, that we are used to

steps.whatToRemember: A sigh breaks the body only over a new sorrow. A sorrow people have grown used to, like the חורבן, does not break them in the same way.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָנֵי מִילֵּי מִילְּתָא חַדְתִּי,
phrases.english: He said to him: This applies only to a new matter,
but this one, which we have gone through again and again, does not.
As people say:
One who is used to losing children does not panic.
phrases.notes: The word in round brackets is in the printed גמרא. The corrected wording in square brackets uses the form for a woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the gentile's challenge in step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every sigh breaks the body, so the Jew should have slowed down.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a new sorrow breaks the body. An old, familiar sorrow does not.

steps.title: Who are the טיילין in the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה, which says the טיילין must be with their wives every day, and asks who they are.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: the טיילין, every day. What does טיילין mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the topic of sighing and returns to the משנה about how often a husband must be with his wife. It asks what the word טיילין means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives different schedules for different kinds of men. To apply the rule for the טיילין, we need to know exactly which men the word covers.

keyTerms.meaning: men of leisure, people who stroll about
a wife's right to marital relations at set times

phrases.english: "The men of leisure: every day."
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה about how often each kind of husband owes his wife marital relations.

phrases.english: What is meant by "men of leisure"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, going back to the wording of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which kind of men the משנה calls טיילין

steps.title: רבא: students who study close to home
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the טיילין are בני פירקי, students who study near home and come back every evening.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: they are students who go to their lessons.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a first answer to the question. The טיילין are students of local Torah lessons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These students study nearby and are home every night, so they can be with their wives daily. This is the first definition, and the next step will challenge it.

phrases.english: רבא said: Students of the lessons.
phrases.notes: He means students who study near home and come back each evening.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The טיילין are students who attend local Torah lessons.

steps.title: אביי: Torah students work too hard to be called men of leisure
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a פסוק that רב יצחק explains as describing the wives of תלמידי חכמים, who lose sleep. Torah students therefore work hard, so how can they be the men of leisure?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: These are the people about whom it says, "It is vain for you who rise early and sit up late, who eat the bread of toil; so He gives to His beloved sleep." רב יצחק said: these are the wives of תלמידי חכמים, who chase sleep from their eyes in this world and reach the life of the next world. And you say they are students of lessons?!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבא's answer. Torah students are not people of leisure at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יצחק reads the פסוק as being about wives of תלמידי חכמים who lose sleep waiting for their husbands, who study late. Since Torah students are busy and away, it makes no sense to call them men of leisure owing their wives every night.

phrases.english: אביי said to him:
These are the ones about whom it is written:
"It is vain for you who rise early and sit up late,
who eat the bread of toil;
so He gives to His beloved sleep."
And רב יצחק said:
These are the wives of Torah scholars,
who chase sleep from their eyes in this world,
and reach the life of the World to Come,
and you say students of the lessons?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: מַאן דִּכְתִיב בְּהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's definition from step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's view that the טיילין are students
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק shows that Torah students work so hard that their wives lose sleep, so they cannot be called men of leisure.

steps.title: אביי following רב: a wealthy man with no worries
steps.stepSummary: אביי instead explains טיילין following רב: a man like רב שמואל בר שילת, who lives off his own wealth in peace, unbothered by the king's tax collector.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: like רב, for רב said: someone like רב שמואל בר שילת, who eats his own food, drinks his own drink, sleeps in the shade of his own home, and the king's tax collector does not pass by his door.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting רבא, אביי gives a new definition of טיילין, based on רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טייל is not a student but a man who is comfortable and free of worry. He has his own food and home, and no one bothers him for taxes. Such a man has the time and strength to be with his wife every day.

keyTerms.meaning: in the shade of his own house

phrases.english: Rather, אביי said: It is like רב's view,
for רב said:
For example, רב שמואל בר שילת,
who eats his own food and drinks his own drink,
and sleeps in the shade of his own house,
and the king's tax collector does not pass by his door.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבא's definition, which step 19 rejected.
steps.terutzMaskana: The טיילין are men who live in comfort without worries.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The טיילין are men who live comfortably off their own means without worries, like רב שמואל בר שילת.

steps.title: רבין: the pampered men of ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: רבין, coming from ארץ ישראל, gives another example of טיילין: the pampered men of the West.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came, he said: for example, the pampered men of the West.
steps.whatsHappening: רבין adds another example of who the טיילין are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבין agrees that a טייל is a comfortable man, and he points to the pampered men of ארץ ישראל. The stories that follow will show how strong those men were.

keyTerms.meaning: the West, a name for ארץ ישראל

steps.whatToRemember: The טיילין are not Torah students. They are comfortable, worry-free men, like רב שמואל בר שילת or the pampered men of ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: When רבין came, he said:
For example, the pampered men of the West.
phrases.notes: "The West" means ארץ ישראל, which is west of בבל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another example to the definition in step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The pampered men of ארץ ישראל are טיילין.

steps.title: רבי אבהו saves himself and two servants
steps.stepSummary: The bathhouse floor collapses under רבי אבהו. He grabs a pillar, climbs up, and pulls up the two servants who were supporting him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו was standing in the bathhouse, and two servants were supporting him. The bathhouse collapsed under him. He came upon a pillar, climbed up, and pulled them up with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story showing how strong the men of ארץ ישראל were.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though servants were holding him up, רבי אבהו was strong enough to save himself and lift both of them. This backs up רבין's point about the men of the West.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ הֲוָה קָאֵי בֵּי בָאנֵי.
phrases.english: רבי אבהו was standing in the bathhouse.
Two servants were supporting him.
The bathhouse collapsed beneath him,
he happened upon a pillar,
he climbed up and pulled them up.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ הֲוָה קָאֵי בֵּי בָאנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates רבין's statement about the men of ארץ ישראל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אבהו was strong enough to save himself and two others.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן saves himself and his two students
steps.stepSummary: A stair breaks under רבי יוחנן. He climbs up and pulls up רב אמי and רב אסי, who were supporting him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן was going up stairs, and רב אמי and רב אסי were supporting him. The stair broke under him. He went up and pulled them up.
steps.whatsHappening: A second story with the same point: a great man of ארץ ישראל shows surprising strength.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like רבי אבהו, רבי יוחנן was being supported, yet he saved the people supporting him. This story also sets up the Rabbis' question in the next step.

phrases.english: רבי יוחנן was going up the stairs,

phrases.aramaic: הֲווֹ סָמְכִי לֵיהּ רַב אַמֵּי וְרַב אַסִּי.
phrases.english: and רב אמי and רב אסי were supporting him.
The stair broke beneath him,
he went up and pulled them up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story parallel to step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן was strong enough to save himself and two others.

steps.title: The Rabbis ask why he needs support
steps.stepSummary: The Rabbis ask רבי יוחנן: if you are this strong, why do you let people support you?
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis said to him: Since you are this strong, why do you need people to support you?
steps.whatsHappening: The Rabbis ask רבי יוחנן a question that comes out of the story. It sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story shows he did not need help walking. So why did he lean on רב אמי and רב אסי at all?

phrases.english: The Rabbis said to him:
Since it is so, that you are this strong,
why does he need to be supported?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about what happened in step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a strong man like רבי יוחנן lets others support him

steps.title: Saving strength for old age
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that if he used up his strength now, he would have nothing left for old age.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: If so, if I use all my strength now, what will I leave for my old age?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the Rabbis and ends the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He lets others support him to save his strength for later in life. His great strength was real, but he chose not to spend it carelessly.
steps.whatToRemember: The stories of רבי אבהו and רבי יוחנן show how strong the men of ארץ ישראל were, which fits רבין's example of the טיילין.

phrases.english: He said to them:

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן מָה אַנִּיחַ לְעֵת זִקְנָה?
phrases.english: If so, what will I leave for the time of old age?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן מָה אַנִּיחַ לְעֵת זִקְנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the Rabbis' question in step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He lets others support him to save his strength for old age.

steps.title: Laborers: twice a week or once a week?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says laborers owe עונה twice a week, but a ברייתא says once a week.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said laborers owe twice a week. But a ברייתא teaches that laborers owe only once a week!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה about פועלים and points out that a ברייתא seems to say something different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives פועלים two times a week. The ברייתא gives them one time a week. Both talk about the same kind of worker, so the numbers clash and need to be explained.

phrases.english: And laborers: twice a week.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה's list of how often each kind of husband owes his wife.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
Laborers: once a week!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the stories about strength and returns to the משנה's list of עונה intervals.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that פועלים owe twice a week
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא gives a different number, once a week, for the same group.

steps.title: Working in their own city versus another city
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא explains that each source is talking about a different case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: This is not a problem. Here they work in their own city, and there they work in another city.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא settles the contradiction by saying the two sources are talking about different workers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A worker who works in his own city comes home every night, so he owes twice a week, like the משנה says. A worker who works in another city is away more, so he owes once a week, like the ברייתא says.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction
Here... there (each source is a different case)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא, לָא קַשְׁיָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, said: It is not difficult:
Here, it is where they work in their own city,
phrases.notes: This 'here' is the משנה, which says twice a week.

phrases.english: there, it is where they work in another city.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן בְּעוֹשִׂין מְלָאכָה בְּעִירָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each source refers to a different situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought both sources described the same laborers, so they contradict.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about workers in their own city (twice a week). The ברייתא is about workers in another city (once a week).

steps.title: A ברייתא that says this split openly
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא spells out the same distinction that רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא made.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this: Laborers owe twice a week. When is this said? When they work in their own city. But when they work in another city, they owe once a week.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same split between one's own city and another city, backing up the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's answer could look like a guess. This ברייתא shows the split is actually taught openly, so both numbers are correct, each in its own case.

keyTerms.meaning: It is also taught this way (a supporting source)
In what case is this said?

steps.whatToRemember: פועלים who work in their own city owe עונה twice a week. If they work in another city, they owe once a week.

phrases.english: This is also taught:
Laborers: twice a week.
In what case is this said?
When they work in their own city,
but when they work in another city,
once a week.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer given in step 27.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's split between own city and another city
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא (תוספתא 5:6) that states the split openly

steps.title: Was the one-week rule only for a טייל and a פועל?
steps.stepSummary: After the משנה gives donkey drivers once a week, רבה בר רב חנן asks אביי whether the earlier one-week vow rule covers only a טייל and a פועל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said donkey drivers owe once a week. רבה בר רב חנן said to אביי: Did the תנא go to all this trouble just to teach us about a man of leisure and a laborer?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה about חמרים. Then רבה בר רב חנן raises a challenge about the earlier rule that a husband who vows off his wife for more than a week must divorce her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a טייל and a פועל owe more often than once a week. Everyone else, like a חמר at once a week or others at once a month, already waits a week or longer. So a one-week vow would not take anything away from those wives. That makes it look as if the תנא wrote the vow rule just for these two kinds of men.

keyTerms.meaning: Donkey drivers who travel with loads
Did the תנא go to all this trouble?
A man of leisure who does not work

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about the חמרים line itself. It is about the earlier משנה on a husband who vows off relations for a week, and whether that rule only matters for a טייל and a פועל.

phrases.english: Donkey drivers: once a week.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבָּה בַּר רַב חָנָן לְאַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Ḥanan said to Abaye:
Did the tanna go to all that trouble to teach us
phrases.notes: Literally, "did the תנא fold himself over," meaning go to great effort. He's pointing back to the one-week vow rule earlier in the משנה.

phrases.english: just a man of leisure and a laborer?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next item in the משנה's list and raises a new challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier משנה that a husband who vows off relations for more than one week must divorce
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Given these intervals, a one-week vow only takes something away from wives of a טייל or a פועל. That seems far too narrow for the תנא to bother teaching.

steps.title: אביי begins his answer: No
steps.stepSummary: אביי starts to answer by denying that the rule is limited to a טייל and a פועל.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: No,
steps.whatsHappening: This is only the opening word of אביי's answer. The גמרא is setting up the explanation, which continues right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By saying 'No,' אביי rejects the idea that the vow rule only covers a טייל and a פועל. His reason comes in the next part of the text.

phrases.english: He said to him: No,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts אביי's reply to רבה בר רב חנן's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejection of the challenge's assumption (the reasoning continues next)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The vow rule seemed to apply only to a טייל and a פועל.
steps.terutzMaskana: אביי denies that limit. His explanation follows.
